{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOLEgSIs8AAAABZbahWg", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bm7fazhDCvVI", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bm7fa", "number": 27, "title": "Stabilize input-source metadata and retained Gamepad lifecycle", "body": "## Problem

Applications retaining XRInputSource metadata or Gamepads encounter inconsistent identities and lifetimes. At dev commit `80dbbf7459862a3306ef51610b8d1c0db1b2de23`, `XRInputSource.profiles` constructs a mutable array on every read, `skipRendering` is absent, and metadata getters read mutable adapter fields. Gamepads also read shared ControllerInput state: ending a session disconnects them temporarily, but starting another session can reconnect and update previously retained objects.

Existing browser tests check within-session Gamepad identity, digital mapping, live collections and shutdown sequencing. They do not establish stable frozen profiles or isolation of retired Gamepads from subsequent sessions.

## Expected outcome

Applications can retain input metadata and sample live controller state reliably. Retired inputs retain their identity and metadata without acquiring later-session state. Preserve Quest controller mapping, deterministic hands and Android transient-touch behavior.

## Context

Target `dev`. Relevant implementation: `src/polyfill/api/runtime.ts`, `src/polyfill/device-adapter.ts`, `src/polyfill/EmulatedXRDevice.ts`, `src/polyfill/api/XRInputSourceArray.ts`; validation: `tests/conformance.ts` and `tests/browser-smoke.ts`. Dependencies include Three.js 0.186.1 and Playwright. The current runner uses Chromium and CDP.

Pinned contracts: [Device CRD, 9 June 2026](https://www.w3.org/TR/2026/CRD-webxr-20260609/#xrinputsource-interface), [Gamepads WD, 7 July 2025](https://www.w3.org/TR/webxr-gamepads-module-1/#gamepad), [WebIDL 622910c](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/whatwg/webidl/622910c67c724e362f71e8255a0380bade261acb/index.bs), and [Gamepad 81ad075](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/w3c/gamepad/81ad0752c4dd06011722b158314eef68cbc2460d/index.html). The dated Gamepads URL was unavailable; the inspected published alias identifies that exact publication.

Correction provenance: the earlier AI assessment treated shared adapter Gamepads as proof that universally distinct cross-session allocation was mandated. Correction: the Gamepads WD guarantees SameObject within a source and defines connection/frame updates, but does not explicitly mandate distinct allocation for every session. Therefore require coherent source-lifetime isolation; per-source wrappers are an implementation policy, not a claimed universal allocation rule.

Issue #11 was administratively closed with broader compatibility work outstanding. PR #26 addressed session-request conversion, not this defect. Its committed report records Chromium 156.0.8078.4 passes; this is implementation-stage evidence, not evaluator execution. Firefox runtime remains untested.

No descriptor is needed for this change. `hand-tracking` retains its existing Quest immersive-only applicability. Additional `tracked-sources` support and virtual haptics remain actionable follow-ups within the fixed goal; this Issue does not complete them or any deferred module.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Return one frozen `profiles` array per source. Preserve existing ordered Quest, hand and touchscreen profiles. Expose readonly input metadata and boolean `skipRendering`; use `false` for current virtual inputs. Preserve stable spaces and existing nullability.
- [ ] Snapshot identity-defining metadata. Changes to handedness, target-ray mode, profiles or Gamepad presence replace the source, with one `inputsourceschange` containing old/new identities after updating the live collection. Button/axis updates preserve source identity.
- [ ] Keep each exposed Quest Gamepad live and SameObject while its source is active. Preserve empty `id`, index `-1`, `xr-standard` mapping, placeholder slots and digital touched/pressed/value behavior. At removal/end, mark it disconnected and retain its final sampled axes/buttons/timestamp. Subsequent input, session restart or profile changes must not reconnect or update that retired exposure. This final-state retention is the selected emulator policy.
- [ ] Preserve touch add/selectstart/select/selectend/remove ordering and one identity per gesture; subsequent gestures use a new source. Retired same-session spaces yield null poses; foreign-session spaces and inactive frames retain `InvalidStateError` behavior.
- [ ] Extend the existing runner with focused assertions across Quest VR, Quest MR and Android AR, plus empty inline input. Cover repeated reads, mutation attempts, multiple frames, removal/reconnection, shutdown while held, restart and profile switching. Exercise hand metadata without changing hand negotiation. Where the panel cannot trigger metadata changes, use a controlled fixture driving the real adapter, without adding a production testing API.
- [ ] The Coordinator runs `npm run build`, `npm run test:browser` and `git diff --check`, recording browser/version, exact coverage, passes, failures and skips. Adapt applicable assertions from pinned WPT input-source identity/recreation/disconnection tests into the existing harness; document native fake-device substitutions and any normative discrepancies. Do not claim verbatim WPT execution.
- [ ] Update the capability inventory and PR with the implemented lifecycle policy and actual execution evidence. Retain the correction above. Any further evidence-backed correction must record the original assumption, correction, primary source and rationale in the Issue/PR, preserving meaningful acceptance without human approval or independent AI re-review. The Coordinator owns implementation, tests and normal PR review.

## Optional validation

Exercise the affected connection/removal behavior through pinned Three.js r186 controller/model consumers. Record source-only inspection separately from execution. Additional WPT adaptation is optional beyond the focused cases above.

## Required post-merge verification

None required.

## Specification reconciliation

This task was authored by AI under the agreed WebXR API compatibility goal for
Quest 3 VR/MR and Android AR. Correct erroneous technical assumptions or acceptance
criteria when primary specifications or measured evidence establish the correction.
Update this Issue and record the original
assumption, corrected requirement, primary reference and rationale in the PR.
These technical corrections require neither human approval nor an independent AI
re-review. Preserve the agreed goal and relevant pre-merge acceptance; do not weaken
requirements merely to accommodate incomplete implementation or failing tests.
